The polling circuit's DOA, DOB, DOC and DOD connections provide information to identify which of the 16 keys has been pressed.
Once the microprocessor has detected the key press, it can then decode the key from an internal look-up table and information from the polling circuit.
After the key is released and the DA signal removed, the flip-flop holds the signal on its output until the microprocessor can read it. In this sense it works as a temporary memory.

The circuit is comprised of two D flip-flops. Flip-flop A is used to show that a key has been pressed. This is driven by a signal of the polling circuit, (DA) which indicates that a key press has occurred and been detected by the polling circuit...
DETECTION AND DECODING
The key detection and decoding circuit, as shown below, allows the microprocessor to detect and identify a pressed key.ey..
The resistors limit current to protect the circuit.

The HIGH input is used in the key detection circuit to indicate a key from the second set of keys. The resistors connected to the supply voltage provide the high condition required when no key is being pressed.
If a key is in second set is pressed, it is also detected by a low on the corresponding Y input but also causes the NAND gate to go HIGH because one of the inputs is now a low.
If a key from the first set is pressed, it is detected by a low on the corresponding Y input and not on the other side of the diode.
The diodes keep the keys of the first set from affecting the NAND gate. Remember, diodes allow current flow in only one direction. During polling, the circuit places a low on the column being tested.

On the 74C922 IC there are four pins, identified as Y1, Y2, Y3 and Y4. These are the horizontal matrix connections and are connected directly to the first four rows of the keypad. The second set of 16 keys are also connected to Y1, Y2, Y3 and Y4, but through diodes...
Normally the circuit can only detect 16 keys, but, with the use of a NAND gate, four resistors and four diodes, the circuit can detect 32.

I/O is arranged in the same way as memory chips. Each address combination of the 8085 address lines can be used by a different device. Most devices will take a range of addresses, not just one.
The ALE pin is used for the address latches and the IO/M pin is what selects between I/O and memory. When this pin is high, it indicates that I/O is being accessed.d.
Also provided to I/O devices are 8 data lines used to transfer information. The direction of data transfer from I/O to the microprocessor is controlled by the WR and RD pins, just as memory is.
Notice there are only 8 address lines used. The 8085 was designed to allow the use of 256 I/O devices. Most computer systems today don't have a need for more than 100 devices.

Many of these signals are used for memory circuit connections. As far as connecting I/O to the 8085, the connections are similar. The main difference is how they are accessed through assembly code. e.
